title: Canada-US Trade Dispute Boosts Maple Syrup Sales
paragraphs: The trade dispute between Canada and the US has had an unexpected effect on one of Canada's most famous products: maple syrup.

In 2025, many Americans bought large amounts of Canadian maple syrup because they expected new tariffs from President Donald Trump's trade war. As a result, Canada's syrup exports rose by nearly 16% in 2025, compared with 9% growth the year before.

However, this rush of buying has created a problem. Quebec, the Canadian province that produces most of the country's maple syrup, keeps a special supply called a "strategic reserve." The reserve is stored in three warehouses that can hold about 218,000 barrels of syrup. It is used to keep supply and prices steady when a harvest is poor. Now, the Quebec Maple Syrup Producers expects the reserve to be completely empty by February.

At the same time, production has fallen in recent years. According to Canada's statistics agency, maple syrup production dropped by 5% in 2025. Exports have also slowed in 2026, growing by only 2.5% in the first eight months of the year.

Canada is by far the world's largest producer of maple syrup today. In 2025, it produced more than 75% of the world's supply, and 90% of Canada's syrup came from Quebec. Quebec has also increased its production capacity by 50% over the past six years, adding more than 21 million new taps to maple trees.

The US remains Canada's biggest customer, buying about 65% of its syrup exports. However, that share has fallen from 80% two decades ago, as Canadian producers have sold more of their syrup to buyers in other parts of the world.
Simon Doré-Ouellet, an official at the Quebec Maple Syrup Producers, said it is clear that the strategic reserve will need to be refilled over the next few years.
